checks.q: Which is NOT one of the three Fundamental Safety Functions?
checks.x: The FSFs are retaining radionuclides, controlling heat generation, and controlling heat removal.

body.text: Functional containment employs diverse passive barriers. They begin at a radionuclide source and include all SSCs between that source and the environment.
body.anchor: begin at a radionuclide source and

items: Maintain at least one barrier beyond the cladding, piping, or vessel containing a source that can reliably withstand LBE and DBA conditions, with leakage specified by design or testing
Keep a minimum total number of required barriers between a source and the environment
Provide a framework for iteration between safety analysis, design, and PRA
body.anchor: The primary goals of the functional containment strategy

body.alt: PSAR Rev 1 figure: Diverse Barriers in Functional Containment

body.text: For the fuel, the cladding provides the first safety-related radionuclide retention barrier.
body.anchor: the cladding provides the first safety-related (SR) radionuclide retention barrier

body.text: The Reactor Enclosure System is the next barrier. Its SR portion includes the reactor head, reactor vessel, and associated component interfaces.
body.anchor: The SR portion of this boundary includes the reactor head, reactor vessel

body.text: The guard vessel provides an additional barrier outside the reactor head and reactor vessel SR boundary.
body.anchor: The guard vessel, also a component of the Reactor Enclosure System, provides an additional barrier

body.text: There are no penetrations through either of the two vessels.
body.anchor: there are no penetrations through either of the two vessels

body.text: A fuel assembly that fails during operation is sealed in an SR canister before storage in the Spent Fuel Pool.
body.anchor: it is sealed in an SR canister prior to storage in the Spent Fuel Pool

body.text: The high boiling point of sodium keeps the core covered by subcooled sodium at near atmospheric pressure during LBEs.
body.anchor: the high boiling point of sodium, which ensures that the reactor core remains covered by subcooled sodium

body.text: The low operating pressure of the primary system and cover gas means there is no significant driving force to transport radionuclides.
body.anchor: ensures there is no significant driving force to transport radionuclides

body.text: Intermediate coolant pressure is greater than primary coolant pressure, so postulated intermediate leaks send sodium into the primary system rather than primary coolant into the intermediate system.
body.anchor: The intermediate coolant pressure is greater than primary coolant pressure

checks.q: Why does a leak between the intermediate and primary sodium result in ingress to the primary system?
o: Intermediate coolant pressure is greater than primary coolant pressure
The IHX is below the sodium level
The cover gas draws sodium in
checks.x: Intermediate coolant pressure is greater than primary pressure, so leaks go into the primary system.
checks.anchor: The intermediate coolant pressure is greater than primary coolant pressure

body.text: Two diverse residual heat removal systems, IAC and RAC, perform functions that satisfy this FSF.
body.anchor: Two diverse residual heat removal systems

cells: Forced flow from the Intermediate Sodium Pump
rows.anchor: One active mode of operation removes heat using the IAC blower and forced flow through the IHT
IAC blower and natural circulation flow in the IHT
passive means of performing the FSF of controlling heat removal using natural draft airflow

body.text: IAC is the primary means of heat removal during plant start-up, shutdown, and off-normal conditions.
body.anchor: is the primary means of heat removal during plant start-up, shutdown, and off-normal conditions

body.text: RAC uses natural circulation of air around the exterior of the guard vessel. It operates continuously, with no operator actions or moving parts required.
body.anchor: The RAC operates continuously, with no operator actions or moving parts required

checks.q: Which system operates continuously with no moving parts or operator actions?
checks.x: RAC operates continuously, with no operator actions or moving parts required to perform its function.
checks.anchor: The RAC operates continuously, with no operator actions or moving parts required

checks.q: What is the primary means of heat removal during start-up, shutdown, and off-normal conditions?

rows.anchor: DL4: Control severe plant conditions and mitigate consequences of BDBEs

body.text: DL1 and DL5 include programmatic elements and design features. DL2, DL3, and DL4 include the design functions needed to ensure performance of the FSFs.

body.text: Among DLs 2, 3, and 4, two independent and diverse DLs, to the extent practicable, can mitigate any AOO postulated initiating event.

body.text: A SARRDL is a prescribed limit of radionuclide release for systems and components.
body.anchor: A SARRDL is a prescribed limit of radionuclide release for systems and components

items: The most limiting LBE does not exceed the siting dose limits at the EAB and LPZ
The 10 CFR 20.1301 annualized dose limits to the public are not exceeded at the EAB for normal operation and AOOs
body.anchor: SARRDLs are established so that

body.text: Compliance comes from monitoring and controlling radionuclide inventory during normal operation, so the assumed inventory at the onset of an LBE is not exceeded.
body.anchor: Compliance with the SARRDLs is achieved through monitoring and controlling radionuclide inventory

o: By operator action after an LBE
By limiting reactor power to 5 percent
By monitoring and controlling radionuclide inventory during normal operation

title: Safety Functions and Defense-in-Depth
subject: safety functions
intro: Every Natrium event lesson comes back to three Fundamental Safety Functions and five Defense Lines. Learn these first.

objectives.text: State the three Fundamental Safety Functions.
Describe the functional containment strategy and its barriers.
Explain how heat generation and heat removal are controlled.
State the five Defense Lines and how independence is achieved between them.
Describe the elements of defense-in-depth evaluation.
